title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
statement: Return the length of the shortest non-empty contiguous subarray with a sum of at least k, or -1 if none exists. The list may contain negative numbers.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(34)
    return [[r.randint(-5, 10) for _ in range(100000)], 5000]

hints.1_question: With negative numbers a sliding window breaks. Think in prefix sums: you want the closest earlier index j with prefix[i] - prefix[j] >= k.
hints.2_nudge: Keep a deque of candidate start indices whose prefix sums are increasing. Pop from the front while the current prefix minus the front's prefix reaches k (record the length), and pop from the back while their prefix is not smaller than the current one.
hints.3_big_hint: For each i in 0..n: while dq and pre[i] - pre[dq[0]] >= k: best = min(best, i - dq.popleft()); while dq and pre[dq[-1]] >= pre[i]: dq.pop(); dq.append(i).

known_bugs.name: sliding window that assumes positive numbers
known_bugs.followup: When a negative number is added, the sum goes down. Does shrinking from the left still find every candidate?

known_bugs.name: never discards larger prefix sums from the back
known_bugs.followup: If an earlier prefix is larger than the current one, can it ever give a better start for a future index than the current one?

known_bugs.name: checks every start index (O(n^2))
known_bugs.followup: How many (i, j) pairs does this try when most subarrays fall short of k? What can a monotonic deque rule out?

followups: Why must the deque keep prefix sums increasing?
Why does popping the front after use never lose a better answer later?
